subject: Monte Carlo Sample Size for CFA

messages.author: 25f4eac5601628b9
messages.subject: Monte Carlo Sample Size for CFA
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to determine my n for CFA with Monte Carlo based on previous research. I set up my population and the null model. However, I get the error message when I try to run simulations:
Error in names(coef) <- lab :
'names' attribute [54] must be the same length as the vector [51]

Here are my models:

pop.model<-'Y1=~0.48*X1+0.65*X2+0.70*X3+0.66*X4+0.74*X5+0.70*X6+0.71*X7+0.77*X8
Y2=~0.81*X9+0.54*X10+0.77*X11+0.85*X12+0.90*X13+0.90*X14+0.78*X15+0.53*X16
Y3=~0.70*X17+0.77*X18+0.55*X19+0.74*X20+0.46*X21+0.52*X22+0.42*X23+0.85*X24
Y1~~0.25*Y2+0.33*Y3
Y2~~0.37*Y3'

null.model<-
'Y1=~X1+X2+X3+X4+X5+X6+X7+X8
Y2=~X9+X10+X11+X12+X13+X14+X15+X16
Y3=~X17+X18+X19+X20+X21+X22+X23+X24
Y1~~Y2+Y3
Y2~~Y3'

analysis300<-sim(nRep=500,model=null.model,n=300,generate=pop.model,lavaanfun="sem",seed=565)

Thanks!!!!

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Monte Carlo Sample Size for CFA
parts:
I believe the issue is in the specification of the latent variances. Since they're not specified in the models they are not being picked up in the sim command. Running a test case of your model it looks like by using a fixed factor method of scale setting you solve this problem (as the latent variances are never free parameters). Try adding std.lv = TRUE to the sim command. That fixed it for me.

Alex
